title: Degreewise exchange compatibility with a morphism of squares and coefficients
statement:
Let $X_0,Y_0,S_0,T_0,X_1,Y_1,S_1,T_1$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $h_b:Y_b\to X_b$, $e_b:Y_b\to T_b$, $f_b:X_b\to S_b$, $g_b:T_b\to S_b$ for $b=0,1$, satisfying $f_bh_b=g_be_b$. Give morphisms $x:X_1\to X_0$, $y:Y_1\to Y_0$, $s:S_1\to S_0$, $a:T_1\to T_0$ satisfying $f_0x=sf_1$, $g_0a=sg_1$, $h_0y=xh_1$, and $e_0y=ae_1$.
Suppose the two squares $f_bh_b=g_be_b$ are cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; the comparison faces need only commute. Let $F_0$ and $F_1$ be abelian sheaves on $(T_0)_{\Et}$ and $(T_1)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $\phi:a^{-1}F_0\to F_1$ be any morphism, and let $q\geq0$. For any commutative face use the degree-$q$ exchange obtained from the bounded below derived mate [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange] applied to the coefficient sheaf in degree zero, using the natural exact-inverse-image cohomology identifications [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Higher direct images mean $R^qu_*G=\mathcal H^q(Ru_*G[0])$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $P^q_{F_0}:s^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\to R^qg_{1,*}a^{-1}F_0$ and $Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\to R^qh_{1,*}y^{-1}e_0^{-1}F_0$ be the comparison-face exchanges. Let $\beta_{b,G}:f_b^{-1}R^qg_{b,*}G\to R^qh_{b,*}e_b^{-1}G$ be the usual higher-direct-image base-change map [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology]. Define
$$ U_\phi=f_1^{-1}(R^qg_{1,*}\phi)\circ f_1^{-1}P^q_{F_0}:x^{-1}f_0^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\longrightarrow f_1^{-1}R^qg_{1,*}F_1, $$
$$ V_\phi=R^qh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\phi)\circ R^qh_{1,*}(\chi_{F_0})\circ Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\longrightarrow R^qh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}F_1, $$
where $\chi:y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$ and the identification $x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\cong f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ in $U_\phi$ are the canonical inverse-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Then
$$ \beta_{1,F_1}\circ U_\phi=V_\phi\circ x^{-1}\beta_{0,F_0}. $$
Neither $\phi$ nor the comparison-face exchanges are required to be isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, affineness or torsion assumption is imposed.

proof.text:
Put $K_0=F_0[0]$ and $K_1=F_1[0]$. Termwise inverse image identifies $a^{-1}K_0$ with $(a^{-1}F_0)[0]$, so $\phi$ gives $\widehat\phi:a^{-1}K_0\to K_1$. All these objects are bounded below. Apply [lem-kun-derived-exchange-cube] to the given eight schemes, their named arrows, and $K_0$. Its four comparison equalities are exactly the four equalities in the hypotheses. With $E_b,P,Q$ denoting the derived exchanges, and $\chi^D:y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\cong e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$, it gives
$$E_{1,a^{-1}K_0}\circ f_1^{-1}P_{K_0}=Rh_{1,*}(\chi^D_{K_0})\circ Q_{e_0^{-1}K_0}\circ x^{-1}E_{0,K_0}.$$
The source comparison $x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\cong f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ is included on the left. The cited cube theorem requires only commuting faces, so no cartesianness of a comparison face is used.

proof.text:
By [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange], $E_1:f_1^{-1}Rg_{1,*}\to Rh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}$ is a natural transformation. Its naturality equation at $\widehat\phi$ is
$$E_{1,K_1}\circ f_1^{-1}Rg_{1,*}(\widehat\phi)=Rh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\widehat\phi)\circ E_{1,a^{-1}K_0}.$$
Precompose with $f_1^{-1}P_{K_0}$ and substitute step 1. Associativity gives
$$E_{1,K_1}\circ f_1^{-1}Rg_{1,*}(\widehat\phi)\circ f_1^{-1}P_{K_0}=Rh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\widehat\phi)\circ Rh_{1,*}(\chi^D_{K_0})\circ Q_{e_0^{-1}K_0}\circ x^{-1}E_{0,K_0}.$$
Only naturality and composition have been used; $\widehat\phi$ is not inverted.

proof.text: Use the natural exact-functor cohomology isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] for each inverse image. Together with the termwise factorization in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], it gives $\lambda_{u,L}:\mathcal H^q(u^{-1}L)\cong u^{-1}\mathcal H^q(L)$ on derived categories: apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the cohomology functors and their isomorphism on complexes. They invert quasi-isomorphisms by the definition of cohomology and exactness. Thus $\lambda$ is natural for derived morphisms as well. These identifications respect the composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Indeed on a representative complex both paths act on cycles by the termwise sheaf composition map and then pass to the quotient by boundaries; the cycle inclusion and cohomology projection compatibility in the exact-functor lemma gives equality. Part (3) of the localization lemma gives the same equality on derived categories. In particular, $\mathcal H^q(\chi^D_L)$ is the sheaf comparison $\chi$ after these identifications.

proof.text: Apply the functor $\mathcal H^q$ to step 2 and use step 3. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $\mathcal H^q(Ru_*G[0])=R^qu_*G$, also on coefficient morphisms by functoriality. The cohomology of $P_{K_0}$ is $P^q_{F_0}$ and that of $Q_{e_0^{-1}K_0}$ is $Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}$, precisely their definitions in the statement. Each square indexed by $b$ is cartesian, and for it $E_b$ is the exchange $\Ex_{\square_b}$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Indeed both are the mate of a square isomorphism under the same adjunctions, by the same unit-isomorphism-counit formula. The sheaf-level $\theta_{\square_b}$ of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] is the identification of both sides with the inverse image along the common composite, i.e. $c^{-1}\circ c$. Hence the component of $\theta^D_{\square_b}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso] at $QK^\bullet$ is the class of the termwise $c^{-1}\circ c$. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], that is also the component of the commutative-square $\theta$. Part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes the two isomorphisms equal, hence also their mates. Therefore [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] identifies $\mathcal H^q(E_{0,K_0})$ with $\beta_{0,F_0}$ and $\mathcal H^q(E_{1,K_1})$ with $\beta_{1,F_1}$. The other three factors become $f_1^{-1}(R^qg_{1,*}\phi)$, $R^qh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\phi)$ and $R^qh_{1,*}(\chi_{F_0})$. Hence the equality obtained is exactly $\beta_{1,F_1}\circ U_\phi=V_\phi\circ x^{-1}\beta_{0,F_0}$. Cartesianness was used only for the two usual-map identifications, and no finiteness, torsion or isomorphism hypothesis was used.

The statement typechecks and the exchange orientations are right. It is exactly what 0ezt uses, with the transition cube and the projection cube and a coefficient morphism that need not be invertible. I tested it on q=0, on the all-identity cube, on phi=0, and on F_0=0 or F_1=0, and it holds in each case. It is not a restatement of the derived cube. Steps 1 to 3 are correct: the cube is applied with its exact face equalities, step 2 is plain naturality, and step 3 makes the cohomology identification natural through localization (2) and (3) and composition clause (2). C4/E5 fault in step 4, fixed: the step applied lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology, which is about Ex_square from def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange, to the cube's E_b, which are commutative-square mates. It never said why the two are the same. I added that argument. theta_square is c^{-1}∘c along fg'=gf' (blueprint_update of def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square, and lem-weil-pbc-square-iso-pasting). Its derived class therefore equals the commutative theta by composition clause (2) and localization (3), and the mates of equal isomorphisms are equal. This is the same repair made to lem-kun-0eym step 5. I added the matching uses and proof_deps. I also declared the tool use lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition, which was off-route and undeclared.
